newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper asks to testify about "narco-jet".
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper asks to testify about "narco-jet".

text.p: President Ernesto Samper told Colombia's chief prosecutor on Wednesday he was eager to give written evidence about the stash of more than eight pounds (3.7 kg) of heroin found aboard his jet.

The "narco-jet" scandal erupted on Sept. 20 after an anonymous phone call and just hours before Samper, already tainted by alleged links to drug barons, was due to fly to New York to address the United Nations general assembly.

In a letter to Alfonso Valdivieso, a fervent anti-drug crusader, Samper wrote: "I'm ready to tell your office about all the facts that I am aware of in relation to this episode. I await receipt of a questionnaire to which I will give my immediate attention."

In comments on Tuesday, a spokesman for the prosecutor's office said there was only a remote possibility that Samper would be called to give evidence in the case. But by early Wednesday local media were reporting that the president would formally be called to testify. In his brief letter, Samper said he only became aware of the decision through the media.

The presidential pilot, also commander of the Catam military air base in Bogota where the Boeing 707 was stationed, was fired on Tuesday as part of the mushrooming inquiry into the heroin discovery. He and 10 other crew members and technicians are still under arrest while investigators hunt for those behind the embarrassing stash.

Samper said just after the discovery of the heroin that it was part of a plot to further muddy his reputation. His administration has been dogged from the outset by allegations that he received millions of dollars in drug money to finance his winning 1994 presidential campaign.
Even though he was cleared of any wrongdoing in June after a congressional inquiry, the United States still withdrew his visa because of what it said were his known links with cocaine traffickers.

Media reports have speculated the heroin may have been planted by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) in a bid to topple Samper, or that high-ranking officers in the Colombian Air Force, in charge of the presidential jet, have teamed up with the Peruvian military to smuggle drugs.
According to the DEA, Colombia has edged out southeast Asia's Golden Triangle as the No. 1 supplier of high grade heroin to the United States.
